speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To begin our evaluation of your hypertension, can you tell me your exact age and height, and have you noticed any headaches, blurred vision, or nosebleeds?

speaker: Patient
text: 5-year-old boy. The patient is presented by his mother for a well-child visit. The boy was born at 39 weeks gestation via spontaneous vaginal delivery, is currently up to date on all vaccines, and is meeting all developmental milestones. His mother reports that he has been generally doing well with no concerns. No family history of cardiovascular disease. The boy does not take any medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history. Since his blood pressure is elevated, I need to determine if this is primary hypertension or secondary to an underlying condition. Have you noticed any swelling in his hands, ankles, or face, or any changes in his urination patterns like foamy urine or reduced frequency?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is High blood pressure on the right upper extremity.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Coarctation of the Aorta.

The finding of elevated blood pressure in the right upper extremity while the lower extremities are likely normotensive (or hypotensive) is classic for coarctation of the aorta. I need to confirm this with imaging and physical exam findings. REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray. REQUEST TEST: Echocardiogram.
